implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.py creates a 3x3 grid of tkinter Buttons inside a Frame (nested loops over range(3) creating buttons for each (row, col)).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Two players alternate placing X and O
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game class in game_logic.py starts with current_player = "X" and toggles it after each successful move (self.current_player = "O" if self.current_player == "X" else "X"). GUI updates status accordingly.
Board.check_winner() in game_logic.py enumerates rows, columns and both diagonals and returns the winning symbol and line when three identical non‑empty marks line up.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect a draw when the board is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_full() checks every cell for non‑EMPTY; Game.handle_move() sets state to STATE_DRAW when board.is_full() is true and no winner.
Game.move_history records tuples (player, row, col) on each successful move; GUI shows the history in _update_move_history().

implemented_requirements.requirement: User‑friendly interface (status, move history, scoreboard, reset)
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.py defines status_label, history_label, score_label and a "Play Again" button; methods _update_status, _update_move_history, _update_scoreboard, and _reset_game manage these UI elements.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends when a player wins or the board is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.state transitions to STATE_WON or STATE_DRAW; GUI disables further clicks and shows a dialog via _show_game_over().

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ability to start a new round without restarting the program
implemented_requirements.evidence: The "Play Again" button calls _reset_game(), which invokes Game.reset() and refreshes the UI.

critical_issues: None observed. The code appears logically correct and all core features are present.
judge.summary: The submitted files provide a complete, functional Tic‑Tac‑Toe implementation. The game logic correctly handles a 3x3 board, turn alternation, win/draw detection, and move history. The Tkinter GUI offers a clear, clickable grid, status messages, move logging, a running scoreboard, win highlighting, and a reset button. No major bugs or missing core functionality were found, and the program is highly likely to run as intended.
